## Abstract

This work explores the application of Active Learning methods to Deep Learning models for instance segmentation of tree species in remote sensing imagery. The goal is to develop an effective method capable of mapping different tree species in forested areas with high precision, even with a limited initial set of annotated data. The proposed approach uses synthetic data generated by the model and validated with morphological information about the trees, in order to improve the learning process and the quality of the predictions. These techniques increased the model's segmentation coverage from 2.35% to 14% of the study area, while keeping the average F1-score high, between 80% and 90%.
